Finan PM.lab_name: Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
Finan PM.sub: Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research · Cambridge, MA, USA
story: The Atlas lists 2 studies with Peter M Finan as a middle author. DIB2012 reports TBC1D7 as the third core subunit of the TSC1-TSC2 complex, the complex that holds back Rheb and mTORC1 (a cell-culture study). DUV2010 reports cells with a permanently active mTORC1 (TSC2 loss), with rapamycin as a control, showing that mTORC1 activation is enough to switch on glycolysis, the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and fat synthesis.

PubMed gives no affiliation for this author in the Atlas papers. The identity was checked through a related paper with several of the same co-authors, which lists Peter M Finan at Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research in Cambridge, Massachusetts, together with co-authors from both Atlas papers. The Atlas papers combine a Harvard group with Novartis scientists.

highlights.DIB2012: Co-author of the study on TBC1D7; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.DUV2010: Co-author of the study on mTORC1 metabolic network; listed in a middle position of the author list.

Beckers J.lab_name: German Mouse Clinic, Institute of Experimental Genetics, Helmholtz Zentrum München (Neuherberg, Germany)
Beckers J.sub: German Mouse Clinic · Helmholtz Zentrum München · Neuherberg, Germany
story: The Atlas lists 2 studies with Johannes Beckers as a middle author. EIS2016 reports oral spermidine extending lifespan in mice, reducing heart enlargement and keeping heart relaxation normal, with the benefit lost in mice whose heart muscle cells lack the autophagy gene Atg5. NEF2013 reports rapamycin extending lifespan in mice while changing only a few classic ageing traits.

The 2013 rapamycin paper lists no affiliation for this author. A later paper from the same mouse-phenotyping group (2020) lists Johannes Beckers at the German Mouse Clinic, Helmholtz Zentrum München, with many of the same co-authors, and the 2016 spermidine record gives the same place. PubMed shows the role of the author only as a place in the author list, so no more is claimed here.

highlights.EIS2016: Co-author of the study on spermidine; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.NEF2013: Co-author of the study on rapamycin ageing screen; listed in a middle position of the author list.

Huynh T.lab_name: Department of Molecular and Human Genetics, Baylor College of Medicine (Houston, Texas, USA)
Huynh T.role: Middle (co-)author of 4 Atlas studies (SET2011, SET2012, SET2013, FER2026).
Huynh T.sub: Baylor College of Medicine · Houston, TX, USA
story: The Atlas lists 4 studies with Tuong Huynh as a middle author. SET2011 reports TFEB driving a coordinated autophagy and lysosome gene programme during starvation. SET2012 reports a signal from the lysosome to the nucleus in which mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of TFEB senses the state of the lysosome. SET2013 reports fasting switching on the TFEB gene in mouse liver, muscle and kidney, with TFEB driving its own transcription in a feed-forward loop that links starvation to lipid metabolism. FER2026 reports kidney-specific mouse models showing that mTORC1 hyperactivation, not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone, is the main driver of kidney cysts and tumours.

The three earlier papers list no affiliation for this author. A 2020 paper from the same group, with co-authors Settembre and Ballabio, lists Tuong Huynh at Baylor College of Medicine and Texas Children's Hospital in Houston, and the 2026 kidney paper gives Baylor as well.

highlights.SET2011: Co-author of the study on TFEB; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.SET2012: Co-author of the study on TFEB lysosome signalling; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.SET2013: Co-author of the study on TFEB feedback loop; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.FER2026: Co-author of the study on kidney cystogenesis; listed in a middle position of the author list.

Shackelford DB.lab_name: Molecular and Cell Biology Laboratory, Dulbecco Center for Cancer Research, Salk Institute for Biological Studies (La Jolla, California, USA)
Shackelford DB.sub: Salk Institute for Biological Studies · La Jolla, CA, USA
story: The Atlas lists 2 studies with David B Shackelford as a middle author. GWI2008 reports a second way AMPK shuts mTORC1 down: AMPK directly phosphorylates Raptor, in addition to acting through TSC2, forming a metabolic checkpoint. EGA2010 reports AMPK directly phosphorylating ULK1, linking energy sensing to autophagy and mitophagy in opposition to mTOR.
The two Atlas records list no affiliation for him. A 2013 paper in Cancer Cell, with co-authors Vasquez and Shaw from the same Salk group, lists David B Shackelford at the Salk Institute in La Jolla.

highlights.GWI2008: Co-author of the study on AMPK-Raptor; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.EGA2010: Co-author of the study on AMPK-ULK1; listed in a middle position of the author list.

Oppliger W.sub: Biozentrum, University of Basel · Basel, Switzerland
story: Wolfgang Oppliger is a middle author on an Atlas study that reports glutaminolysis activating Rag-mTORC1 signalling through alpha-ketoglutarate (a cell-culture study). The Atlas record lists no affiliation for him. A 2014 paper from the same Basel group, with co-authors Robitaille and Hall, lists Wolfgang Oppliger at the Biozentrum of the University of Basel. Two other Atlas studies under this name (LOE2002, ZIN2011) could not be tied to him and are left out.

highlights.DUR2012: Co-author of the study on glutaminolysis; listed in a middle position of the author list.
